content: ESA - Chaotic crust contains clues to Mars’ watery past Science & Exploration Chaotic crust contains clues to Mars’ watery past 31/08/2022 7652 views 131 likes ESA / Science & Exploration / Space Science / Mars Express Mars Express takes us over the Holden Basin – part of a region that is a high-ranking target in the search for signs of past life on the Red Planet. This image was taken on 24 April 2022 by the spacecraft’s High Resolution Stereo Camera. A barren landscape shaped by water The broader region The Holden Basin* is part of a series of channels and sinks called the Uzboi-Ladon-Morava (ULM) outflow system that may have once drained up to 9% of the martian surface. The complex history of the ULM outflow system makes it an interesting target to explore in more detail with Mars orbit
